item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports separating interests across temporal scales. **MSMT-LSI (2024)** combines multihead attention with long- and short-term temporal embeddings; **IBLSRec (2025)** distinguishes stable item relationships from transient interactions and uses inferred intent to refine preferences, explicitly targeting sparsity. **MIMAR-SRec (AAAI 2026)** models intent across contextual windows, aligns representations with intent prototypes, and adds robustness to interaction and temporal noise. These papers treat intent as learned from behavior, rather than observed psychological traits. Sources: [MSMT-LSI](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5), [IBLSRec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/), [MIMAR-SRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489).\n\nMixture-of-experts offers complementary mechanisms. **HyMoERec (2025 preprint; AAAI 2026 student abstract)** combines a shared dense expert with sparse specialized experts and learnable fusion. **Mixture of Sequence (WWW 2026)** routes histories into latent themes and combines global, short-term, and theme-specific experts. **TriSSR (2026)** adaptively fuses sequence, frequency-scale, and temporal-interval experts. A practical inference for this benchmark: retain SASRec as the recent-context branch, add masked full-history pooling and a small latent-intent expert bank, then learn a gate conditioned on context, history length, and available time gaps. Sparse-history benefits remain a hypothesis; compare against simpler two-branch fusion using the common macro validation HR@10, and inspect gate saturation and expert utilization. Sources: [HyMoERec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.06388), [Mixture of Sequence](https://q-rz.github.io/static/www26/www26-mos-paper.pdf), [TriSSR](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925231226009707)."}
